title: Beyond Coherence: Improving Temporal Consistency and Interpretability in Dynamic Topic Models
subcategory: LLM-augmented neural dynamic topic model with optimal transport
task: Dynamic topic modelling of timestamped corpora
problem: Dynamic NTM encoders ignore PLM semantics, temporal links are rigid one-to-one chains (no splits/merges), and top-word interpretability is shallow.
architecture: L-DNTM: variational dynamic NTM with (i) multi-objective distillation (InfoNCE between topic proportions and PLM embeddings plus a CKA structural loss), (ii) entropic optimal transport aligning the full set of topics between adjacent time slices, and (iii) LLM-guided refinement of topic-word distributions through a KL loss; OT and LLM terms start after warm-up.
llm_or_encoder: Pretrained language model embeddings for distillation; an LLM for topic-word refinement

datasets.name: WHO
datasets.details: weekly WHO articles, January-May 2020, shorter documents

metrics: Topic Quality TQ = TC x TD
key_results: DTQ on NeurIPS 0.359 vs 0.317 for BERTopic; on NYT 0.422 vs 0.349 for CFDTM.
Static topic coherence C_V 0.594 (NeurIPS), 0.554 (ACL) and 0.629 (NYT) with diversity 0.841, 0.853 and 0.862.
On WHO, BERTopic is best across metrics (DTQ 0.275 vs 0.260 for L-DNTM).
strengths: Handles topic splits and merges through set-level OT alignment instead of one-to-one chains.
Improves coherence and diversity together; results averaged over five runs with significance tests.

limitations.text: PLM distillation adds bias and computational overhead.
Optimal transport is costly for many topics or long time horizons.
LLM refinement needs repeated prompting, which limits scalability and may propagate errors.
Experiments are restricted to English corpora.
In the ablation, the variant without the LLM component has higher TQ and TTC than the full model on NeurIPS and NYT.

notes: K = 50 topics; five runs; preprocessing with TopMost.
